s6.title: Create Classes, Fields & Instances

questions.question: Why declare name before assigning this.name?
options: It gives every User instance a checked name field
It hides the field at runtime
questions.explanation: The class declaration establishes the instance shape that constructor assignments must satisfy.

questions.question: What does new User('Max', 36) do?
options: Creates an instance and runs its constructor
questions.explanation: The new operator allocates an object linked to the class and invokes its constructor.

s6.title: Use Parameter Properties & Access Modifiers

questions.question: What turns a constructor parameter into an instance field?
options: An access modifier such as public or private
questions.explanation: A modifier on a constructor parameter activates TypeScript's parameter-property shorthand.

questions.question: Where may a private age field be read?
questions.explanation: Private members are checked so only their declaring class can access them.

s6.title: Protect State with readonly, Accessors & Static Members

questions.question: Why can a readonly hobbies array still accept push()?
options: readonly protects the property binding, not the mutable array contents
questions.explanation: Readonly is shallow unless the referenced value is also modeled as readonly.

questions.question: How is a getter named fullName accessed?
questions.explanation: Getter syntax exposes a computed value as a property.

s6.title: Build Inheritance with super & protected

questions.question: Why must Employee call super()?
questions.explanation: The base constructor must initialize the inherited portion of the instance.

questions.question: Who may access a protected member?
options: The declaring class and its subclasses
questions.explanation: Protected keeps outside callers out while allowing derived classes to collaborate with the base class.

s6.title: Design Abstract Base Classes

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an abstract class?
options: Serve as a non-instantiable base for concrete subclasses
questions.explanation: Abstract classes centralize shared implementation while requiring callers to construct a concrete subtype.

questions.question: What must SideDrawerElement pass to super?
options: Nothing, even when the base requires data
questions.explanation: Subclass constructors must satisfy the base constructor's parameter contract.

s6.title: Define & Use Interface Object Contracts

questions.question: What belongs inside an interface method declaration?
options: Its parameter and return types, without a body
questions.explanation: Interfaces describe behavior contracts rather than implementing behavior.

questions.question: What must an object typed Authenticatable provide?
questions.explanation: Structural typing checks the object's complete required shape.

s6.title: Compare Interfaces, Type Aliases & Callable Contracts

questions.question: What does interface declaration merging do?
options: Combines compatible declarations with the same interface name
Converts an interface to a class
questions.explanation: Repeated interface declarations contribute members to one resulting contract.

questions.question: Which syntax is more commonly used for a plain function contract?
questions.explanation: Interfaces can be callable, but function type aliases are typically easier to recognize.

s6.title: Implement Interfaces & Depend on Minimum Shapes

questions.question: May an implementing class have members not listed by the interface?
options: Yes, implements enforces a minimum shape
questions.explanation: The interface requires members but does not forbid additional class-specific behavior.

questions.question: Why type authenticate with Authenticatable instead of AuthenticatableUser?
options: It accepts any value with the required capability
It emits the interface at runtime
questions.explanation: Depending on the contract decouples the function from a specific implementation.

s6.title: Extend Interfaces & Understand Type Erasure

questions.question: How does extends differ from declaration merging here?
options: extends creates a new derived interface
questions.explanation: The base remains unchanged while the derived interface adds or combines requirements.

questions.question: What happens to interface declarations in emitted JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Interfaces are compile-time-only TypeScript constructs.

s7.title: Compose Shapes with Intersection Types

questions.question: What must AccessedFileData contain?
questions.explanation: An intersection combines requirements rather than choosing one branch.

questions.question: What is the interface equivalent of combining these shapes?
options: An interface extending FileData and Status
questions.explanation: Interface inheritance can combine multiple object contracts.

s7.title: Narrow Union Objects with Type Guards

questions.question: Why check 'path' in source?
options: It supplies runtime evidence that narrows to FileSource
It converts the object to a file
It adds path to every object
questions.explanation: The in operator verifies property existence at runtime and TypeScript follows that control flow.

questions.question: Why is source.connectionUrl safe after the early return?
options: The FileSource branch has already exited
questions.explanation: Control-flow analysis knows the remaining path must be the database branch.

s7.title: Model Exhaustive Branches with Discriminated Unions

questions.question: What makes this union discriminated?
options: Every member has a shared type field with a distinct literal value
questions.explanation: The common literal tag connects runtime branching to static narrowing.

questions.question: Why call assertNever in default?
options: To detect an unhandled future union member
questions.explanation: Exhaustiveness checking fails when source is no longer never.

s7.title: Reuse instanceof & Custom Type Predicates

questions.question: When is instanceof an appropriate guard?
questions.explanation: Instanceof checks the runtime prototype chain of class instances.

questions.question: What does source is FileSource mean?
options: A true result tells TypeScript the argument is FileSource
questions.explanation: A type predicate attaches narrowing information to the Boolean result.

s7.title: Map Inputs to Outputs with Function Overloads

questions.question: What information do overloads preserve?
options: The relationship between each input form and its output type
questions.explanation: Each overload signature maps a supported argument type to a precise return type.

questions.question: How many implementation bodies may an overloaded function have?
questions.explanation: Several visible signatures share one compatible implementation.

s7.title: Model Dynamic Keys with Index Signatures & Record

questions.question: What does [property: string]: number | boolean allow?
options: Any string-compatible key whose value is number or boolean
Only a property literally named property
questions.explanation: The bracketed name is a placeholder for dynamic string keys.

questions.question: Which utility describes the same broad dictionary?
questions.explanation: Record maps an allowed key type to an allowed value type.

s7.title: Preserve Literal Values with as const

questions.question: What is the inferred type of roles[0] after as const?
questions.explanation: A const assertion preserves positional literal information in the tuple.

questions.question: How does as const differ from a const variable declaration?
options: It also narrows literals and makes inferred members readonly
questions.explanation: Const prevents rebinding; a const assertion affects the inferred type of the value.

s7.title: Validate Contracts without Losing Inference

questions.question: What does satisfies preserve that a broad annotation can lose?
options: The value's specific inferred keys and literals
questions.explanation: Satisfies checks compatibility without replacing the expression's useful inferred type.

questions.question: Does satisfies transform or validate data at runtime?
options: No, it is a compile-time compatibility check
questions.explanation: Runtime validation needs separate JavaScript logic or a validation library.
